title: Operator runbook: Quiet cutovers and automated fallback orchestration for private deployments
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This runbook describes the operator-facing procedures for performing quiet cutovers (low-noise, low-risk upgrades), controlled canary rollouts, and automated fallback orchestration for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It combines preflight checks, phased traffic steering, automated health gates, and forensic-safe rollback so field engineers can perform upgrades with minimal impact to customer SLAs.

Scope:
- Applies to: Private control plane and tenant-serving runtime upgrades, model swaps, and runtime configuration changes in VPC and air-gapped on-prem installs.
- Not covered: full datacenter evacuations and vendor hardware recall processes (see field-handoff docs).

Owner & escalation:
- Runbook owner: Platform Delivery (eng-private-deployments)
- Primary oncall: Private Deploy SRE rotation
- Escalation path: Private Deploy SRE -> Runtime Team Lead -> Head of Platform -> Customer Success (for customer comms)

Key definitions:
- Quiet cutover: A staged upgrade that minimizes telemetry noise and user-visible errors by using small traffic steps, proactive cache warming, and KV-prefix preservation techniques.
- Fallback orchestration: Automated change that routes traffic back to the last-known-good model/version/pool when health gates fail.
- Health gate: A programmatic condition (latency, error rate, token loss, output regression) that must be met before advancing rollout.

Preflight checklist (complete before any cutover):
1) Stakeholder notifications: notify Customer Success and account owner if cutover affects customer SLA boundaries.
2) Snapshot state: take KV/cache snapshot and model version manifest:
   - CLI: `redwoodctl snapshot kv --tenant <TENANT_ID> --out /tmp/kv-snap-<TIMESTAMP>.tar.gz`
3) Capacity & cadence: ensure at least 20% spare serving slots across the target pool or pre-provision burst nodes.
4) Telemetry baseline: capture 30m baselined metrics for the target route(s):
   - LAT_p50/p95, tokens/sec, errors/min, model_quality_score (if enabled)
5) Run quick regression eval set locally for new model variant (if model swap): `eval-harness run --suite smoke-small --model new-model:tag`
6) Confirm artifact signatures for on-prem images (airgapped): verify SHA256 and sigstore attestations.

Health gate thresholds (recommended defaults; tune per-customer):
| Metric | Gate type | Threshold to advance | Threshold to abort and rollback |
|--------|-----------|----------------------|----------------------------------|
| p95 latency | safety | <= baseline * 1.25 | > baseline * 1.5 for 5m |
| errors/min | safety | <= baseline + 3 | >= baseline + 10 for 3m |
| requests with degraded output | quality | <= 1% | >= 3% for 10m or failing smoke evals |
| token amplification | cost | <= 1.2x baseline | >= 1.5x sustained 10m |

Note: Baseline values must be computed from preflight telemetry (last 30m steady-state).
